n: In the eleventh year, after several peaceful years, a cry of war suddenly rings through the land on a specific date — the fifth day of the second month.

f.g: The sudden end to a period of peace.

n: Lamanite armies come in from the wilderness and strike Ammonihah first, killing its people and destroying the city — exactly as Alma had warned.
Before the Nephites can gather enough soldiers, Ammonihah is destroyed, some around Noah are killed, and others are taken captive.
The Nephites want to rescue the captives taken into the wilderness.

f.w: obtain those who had been carried away

n: Zoram, the chief captain, and his sons Lehi and Aha, ask Alma — as a prophet — where the Lord wants them to search.

f.g: A Nephite military leader, not to be confused with Laban’s servant (1 Nephi 4:35) or the Zoramites of Alma 31.

n: Alma asks the Lord and reports: the Lamanites will cross the Sidon in the south wilderness beyond Manti; meet them there on the east side and the Lord will deliver the captives.
Zoram and his sons follow the prophet’s directions exactly.

f.g: Unsettled land to the south, toward the Lamanite regions.

n: They scatter the Lamanites and rescue every captive — not one was lost — and bring them home.

f.w: not one soul of them had been lost

n: The eleventh year ends with the Lamanites driven out — but Ammonihah, the great city its people thought God could not destroy, has been completely wiped out.

f.w: which they said God could not destroy

n: In one day the city was left empty, the bodies torn by dogs and wild animals — fulfilling the warning that it would be destroyed “in one day.”
Eventually the bodies were piled up and thinly covered. The stench kept people away for years, and the place was called “Desolation of Nehors.”
The Lamanites don’t return to war until the fourteenth year, giving the Nephites three years of peace.
Alma and Amulek preach in temples, sanctuaries, and synagogues, which the Nephites built in the Jewish style.

f.w: synagogues, which were built after the manner of the Jews
f.g: Synagogue = a local house of assembly and worship.

n: They teach everyone who will listen, without favoritism.
Many others join the work, and the church becomes established throughout Nephite lands.
There was no inequality among them. The Lord poured out his Spirit everywhere to prepare hearts for his coming.
The aim: that people might not harden their hearts, but receive the word with joy and be grafted like a branch into the true vine — Christ.
The priests preach against lying, envy, strife, theft, violence, adultery, and lust.
They proclaim what is coming: Christ’s birth, suffering, death, and resurrection.
People ask where Christ will appear and learn he will visit them after his resurrection — joyful news fulfilled in 3 Nephi 11.

f.w: he would appear unto them after his resurrection

n: With the church established, the devil overcome for a time, and the word preached in purity, the fourteenth year ends in blessing.
